doc.title: John Levy interviewed by Monk Rowe, Majesty of the Seas, May 31, 1995

title: Building Joe Williams's small group and continuing work with the Basie band
summary: After Basie, Joe Williams formed small jazz groups, settling on a trio, and still guests with the Basie band several times a year.

story.theme_name: Singers and the musicians who accompanied them
story.community_name: Joe Williams: the singer with Basie

blocks.x: That’s great. When you first started working with Joe then, he had come out of that period where he’d had the hit with the Basie band. Was there a conscious decision with you guys at that point where you said okay, I did the big band thing, now I’m ready for a solo career, or did you find a group to play with him or was he kind of freelancing with different bands?

No, no, no, no, no. He went right into, went pretty much right into a group thing, you know. I think it was Junior Mance was one of the first pianists, and then later on he had several different pianists, I can’t recall exactly in what order and who was there. Joe probably told you that story. But it was a conscious effort to put together a group but it was like a small jazz group, because that was what was the popular thing at the time. So I remember Sweets Edison was in the group, and there’s a tenor player, I can’t recall his name was in the group for a while with us. And we used different people, you know. And finally after several years of mixtures of different musicians and everything, he settled pretty much on a standard trio thing, along with maybe adding a guitar here and there or adding a horn here and there. And you know, used as the basis for his, which is still the system. But still, when the Basie band was still on the road and going, he had to do a lot of things, at least there was a lot of offers, because the relationship was excellent with Basie. So there was a lot of times where you know they’d make offers to us, the agencies would make offers for us to join the Basie band for a special or a festival.

So we kept working with the Basie band and that exists until today. We still work maybe two and three and sometimes as many as four different times a year with the Basie band. And what we do then, we just take his own, Norman Simmons, his pianist, and then work within the context of the Basie band. And we do quite a few of those things. In fact we’re going to be going to play the Montreal festival this year, Toronto festival this year, back to back with the Basie band. And we’ve got an offer on the table now to go to Poland with the Basie band, and I’ll know when I get back. Because I don’t want to know about any business when I’m on this —
That’s a major project I guess.
